evidence.observation: The plan defines the key as `(address, canonical JSON of the offending row)` and says an id-less constraint uses a positional address. It also requires that the `key survives inserting a rule above another`, while RC-D4 says `key by positional address` and calls it `unstable`. Inserting a rule changes that address.

concerns.recommendation: Require declared ids for baseline comparison, or define a stable identity for id-less constraints; make RC3-C4 cover both cases explicitly.
concerns.title: Baseline keys cannot survive rule insertion for id-less constraints

evidence.observation: RC3 addresses `when either run is undecided`, and RC3-C3 excludes an `undecided alethic verdict` from a no-new-violations claim. The plan separately says vacuous verdicts are a `shortfall` and need `--allow-vacuous` to move band 2 to 0. It gives no baseline outcome when either run is vacuous without that option.

concerns.recommendation: Specify and test baseline behavior for vacuous head and base runs, so an unaccepted vacuous run cannot produce a no-new-violations claim.
concerns.title: Baseline can claim no new violations after a vacuous run

evidence.location: Binding rule 7, lines 93-97; §2.4, lines 172-176; dependencies, lines 186-194
evidence.observation: The plan says `New meaning goes in version 15 only`, but RC4 says `the payload records that the option was used` and is `independent` of RC1. Without RC1's version 15, recording that option changes an existing report variant.

concerns.recommendation: Route `--allow-vacuous` through version 15 and make RC4 depend on RC1, or explicitly design another new report variant.
concerns.title: Independent RC4 conflicts with frozen report variants

evidence.observation: RC1 defines version 15 as the version-7 shape `with three more required verdict keys: address, addressing and remedy`. RC3 then says `Each version-15 verdict gains an aligned novelty list` and adds a top-level baseline block. The existing report schema uses closed verdict shapes, so RC3 changes the version-15 contract after RC1-C5 validates it.

concerns.recommendation: Define the complete fixed version-15 shape in RC1, including baseline defaults and novelty fields, and validate both ordinary and baseline payloads against it.
concerns.title: Version 15 changes shape between RC1 and RC3

evidence.observation: RC-D5 proposes `exit 0, outcome accepted, acceptance_ready: false` for standing-only violations, while RC3-C2 checks only that `the band follows the RC-D5 ruling`. In the cited existing payload contract, `acceptance_ready` is true exactly when exit code is 0; `src/gnd/payloads.py` implements it as `exit_code == 0`.

concerns.recommendation: Define the version-15-specific meaning and builder behavior for `acceptance_ready`, then add a standing-only JSON assertion to RC3-C2.
concerns.title: Standing-only acceptance contradicts the current payload invariant

evidence.location: RC2-C4, line 225; RC3-C5, line 236; RC6, lines 251-256; verification table, lines 303-312
evidence.observation: RC2-C4 says only `time bound over 2,000+ edges`, RC3-C5 says `time bound over 2,000+ rows`, and RC6 says its `exact gate` is unresolved. No numerical limits or stop conditions are stated for the phases, so those criteria cannot yet fail on elapsed time or bounded work.

concerns.recommendation: Set measurable time or work ceilings, test conditions, and a stop condition for each phase before its owner gate.
concerns.title: Phase budgets and stop conditions are not falsifiable

response.summary: The plan has unresolved contradictions in baseline identity and report-version behavior, and its execution bounds are not yet measurable.
